open_questions: Could radial-velocity mass limit still formally allow brown-dwarf-mass companion with measured phase 0.7431 eclipse, but secondary depth and duration already establish stellar companion
dossier.public_summary: The light curve shows a second eclipse almost as deep as the transit itself and transit depths that jump from ~600 ppm to ~6600 ppm across sectors. A planet on the small M-dwarf would have a short steady dip, but the long, variable, off-phase deep eclipse is the eclipse of a small star blended with the target. Together with the very long transit duration this is an eclipsing binary, best explained as a diluted stellar binary, not a planet.

reasons.why: Deep secondary at ~0.74 phase with depth >50% of dip. Not a hot-Jupiter occultation; star-density units and magnitude point to secondary eclipse of a stellar companion on target. TESS rules for stellar vs planetary secondary are met with low vs high depth_over_dip and snr 5.652 >> best_brightening_snr 3.38.
reasons.value: snr 5.652 at phase 0.7431, depth_ppm 2042, depth_over_dip 0.5425, secondary_over_bump 1.672

reasons.why: Transit depths differ by factor ~11 between sectors (1857 ppm in sector 10 vs 6603 ppm in sector 100) with same-source variation significant. A planet on the target must be steady; this is variability of a blend/EB, not aperture calibration.

Transit is much longer than central duration expected for the 0.3575 Rsun M-dwarf. Together with inflated depths in some sectors indicates blended eclipses diluted to planet size, consistent with small-star eclipses rather than a planet.
reasons.value: observed_h 3.498 vs central_h 2.204 ratio 1.588, star_density_penalty 38.93, fit_log_density_ratio -0.679

reasons.why: Machine-learning planet ranking is in the bottom decile, as observed for false positives. Low rank plus long duration, secondary and variable depth together favour non-planet, despite flat shape v_sigma -1.573 and no odd/even difference diff_sigma 1.068.
Aperture-size dependent depth changes support blended/variable EB even without an on-target centroid; plausible_within_1px 0 rules out 1-pixel neighbour but leaves on-target stellar binary/blend.
